name: Pydantic v2 models validation serialization
short_definition: Pydantic v2 is the default runtime validation and serialization layer for Python services: BaseModel schemas coerce and guarantee output types via pydantic-core (Rust), emit JSON Schema for OpenAPI, and integrate with FastAPI request/response models. Prefer model_validate / model_dump over V1 parse_obj / dict APIs.
scope_in: BaseModel ConfigDict Field field_validator model_validator computed_field TypeAdapter RootModel; model_validate model_validate_json model_dump model_dump_json model_json_schema; aliases validation_alias serialization_alias; strict mode; from_attributes ORM mapping; ValidationError handling; FastAPI body/query/response models; generic models and PEP 695 type params.
scope_out: pydantic-settings (see py-settings-config); msgspec hot-path codec (see py-msgspec-hotpath); full ORM design; Pydantic AI agents; hand-written JSON Schema without models; V1 BaseSettings/Config classes as greenfield defaults.
defaults: Always Pydantic v2 APIs (model_* methods, ConfigDict, SettingsConfigDict elsewhere). Request/response DTOs: BaseModel with explicit Field constraints (min_length, ge/le, patterns). External JSON: model_validate_json when payload is raw bytes/str; model_validate for dicts. Response: model_dump(mode='json') or model_dump_json for wire. API ingress models use extra='forbid' to reject unknown keys. Internal domain models may use extra='ignore'. Prefer SecretStr for secrets in models. Use TypeAdapter for non-model types (list[Item], unions). from_attributes=True for ORM→DTO. Prefer concrete list/dict over Sequence/Mapping for performance. Enable strict=True only at trusted boundaries where coercion is dangerous (IDs, money). Pin pydantic>=2.13,<3 as of 2026-07.
decision_gates: USE when: untrusted input (HTTP, webhooks, queue messages, LLM tool args, env-shaped nested JSON); need OpenAPI/JSON Schema; FastAPI integration; need field-level errors for clients. DO NOT USE when: pure internal typed code with no I/O boundary (prefer dataclasses/attrs + static types); ultra-hot pure encode/decode loops where profiling shows model_validate dominates (consider msgspec); binary protocols (prefer protobuf). Prefer TypeAdapter over one-off BaseModel wrappers for single-type validation. Prefer RootModel for top-level list/dict roots. Prefer annotated constraints over ad-hoc validators when Field/Annotated covers it.
do_dont: DO: model_validate / model_validate_json for ingress; model_dump(mode='json') for egress; ConfigDict(extra='forbid') on public API models; Field(description=...) for OpenAPI; field_validator(mode='after') for domain rules; model_validator(mode='after') for cross-field rules; ValidationError.errors() for structured error maps; separate In/Out models when shapes differ; frozen=True for value objects you pass around. DON'T: use .dict() / .json() / parse_obj / parse_raw / from_orm / Config class (V1); mutate shared model instances as global state; put DB sessions or clients on models; catch Exception and swallow ValidationError without mapping; use model_construct on untrusted data; custom __init__ that skips super validation; abstract Sequence/Mapping as default field types for hot validation; serialize secrets without redaction.
failure_modes: 1) Silent extra fields accepted (default extra='ignore') → clients send typos that never apply. 2) Lax coercion surprises ("123"→int, floats truncated to int) at money/ID boundaries. 3) V1 APIs in agent-generated code break at runtime under v2. 4) from_attributes missing → ValidationError on ORM objects. 5) model_construct used for untrusted queue payloads → invalid state in DB. 6) Recursive models without model_rebuild → incomplete schema / OpenAPI failures. 7) Serializing SecretStr/API keys into logs via model_dump. 8) Over-broad Union models causing slow/ambiguous validation. 9) Nested ValidationError not mapped → 500 instead of 422. 10) Sharing mutable model instances across requests.
anti_patterns: BaseModel.Config nested class; parse_obj/parse_raw/from_orm/dict()/json(); arbitrary types without validation (arbitrary_types_allowed as default); dumping full models into structured logs; using the same model for DB row, API in, and API out when fields differ; validators with side effects (network/DB); raising HTTPException inside pure validators; putting Optional everywhere instead of required fields; TypedDict for untrusted HTTP bodies when BaseModel is available; dynamic create_model from user-controlled strings without allowlists.
tools: Primary: pydantic + pydantic-core. Runtime consumers: FastAPI, pydantic-settings, SQLAlchemy DTO mapping, httpx response parsing via TypeAdapter. Alternatives: msgspec (hot path encode/decode), attrs+cattrs (internal), dataclasses+manual checks (small scripts), jsonschema (schema-only, no models). Dev: basedpyright for static types; pytest + pytest-pydantic-error or plain ValidationError asserts; ruff rules for unused imports around models.
versions_as_of: as_of 2026-07-13: pydantic v2.13.4 (docs latest); pydantic-core ships with pydantic; Python 3.12–3.14 target per stack. Greenfield pin: pydantic>=2.13.0,<3. FastAPI versions that require pydantic v2 only (do not install pydantic v1). Note v2.13 adds polymorphic serialization and related features — prefer latest 2.13.x patch.
config_snippets:
# pyproject.toml
[project]
dependencies = [
  "pydantic>=2.13.0,<3",
  "fastapi>=0.115",
]

# ruff: no special pydantic plugin required for v2
# CI: basedpyright must type-check BaseModel fields; pytest covers ValidationError paths

# optional: strict for critical models
# model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True, extra='forbid')
deprecation_watch: Pydantic V1 APIs: .dict(), .json(), parse_obj, parse_raw, from_orm, update_forward_refs, class Config, allow_mutation (use frozen), orm_mode (use from_attributes). pydantic.v1 namespace is migration-only — never greenfield. Avoid teaching agents V1 FastAPI examples from old blogs. Avoid root __root__ field style — use RootModel. Avoid copy() update patterns without model_copy(update=...).
ts_boundary: Python Pydantic models are the source of truth for FastAPI OpenAPI; generate TS types/Zod from OpenAPI (openapi-typescript or similar), do not hand-sync interfaces. Next.js BFF should treat Python service responses as untrusted JSON and re-validate with Zod at the BFF edge if reshaping. Prefer camelCase serialization aliases only if the public contract is camelCase — document alias policy once. Shared domain names: User, Organization — keep field parity in OpenAPI components.
rust_boundary: Hand off to Rust (Axum + serde) when: multi-GB JSON throughput, sub-ms validation SLOs, or CPU-bound transform pipelines. Keep Pydantic at the Python AI/worker boundary. For dual services, OpenAPI or JSON Schema is the contract — do not share Pydantic models with Rust. Binary hot paths: protobuf/msgpack with schema registry rather than free-form Pydantic JSON.
supabase_boundary: Do not treat PostgREST row shapes as trusted without validation when they enter Python workers. Map selected columns into BaseModel DTOs; avoid model_validate(entire_row) if RLS views expose extra columns you must not process. Prefer explicit field lists. Service-role clients must still validate outbound writes. Migrations remain SQL-first (Alembic/Supabase); Pydantic is not the migration source of truth.
boundary_contracts: Emit OpenAPI from FastAPI (Pydantic → JSON Schema). Version /v1 paths. Env vars for model-related feature flags are plain settings, not BaseModel secrets. Export model_json_schema() into contract tests. MCP tool args: validate with BaseModel/TypeAdapter before side effects. Queue message envelopes: {schema_version, payload} with versioned models.
decision_matrix_row: Problem: validate untrusted JSON / emit OpenAPI schemas / FastAPI bodies → Python+Pydantic. Problem: BFF request validation next to React forms → TypeScript+Zod. Problem: extreme throughput JSON gateways or multi-service mesh contracts → Rust+serde or protobuf. Problem: browser-only form UX → TS only. Prefer one runtime validator per language boundary; never skip validation because 'the other side used Pydantic'.
threats: Mass assignment via extra fields when extra='allow' or ignore-with-side-effects; prototype pollution-style unexpected keys in nested dicts; type confusion via lax coercion (string IDs becoming ints); secret leakage in model_dump/logs/errors (input_value in ValidationError); ReDoS-like expensive validators on huge strings; deserializing untrusted pickles disguised as models (never pickle models); ImportString / dynamic create_model from user input → code execution; SSRF if URL fields not constrained; prompt-injection payloads accepted as 'valid' strings into LLM tools.
mitigations: extra='forbid' on public models; size limits (max_length, max_items); constrain URLs/hosts with allowlists; SecretStr and exclude secrets from dumps; strip or redact input_value in client-facing error mappers; never model_construct on untrusted data; avoid ImportString in user-facing settings; bound recursion depth for nested models; validate after authz (know who is writing); schema_version on envelopes; CI contract tests that reject extra properties.
agent_codegen_policy: MUST generate: ConfigDict (not class Config); model_validate/model_dump; extra='forbid' for public API models; Field constraints; typed ValidationError handling at edges; separate In/Out models when needed; from_attributes for ORM DTOs. MUST NOT generate: V1 methods; model_construct for request bodies; print(model) of secrets; arbitrary_types_allowed without review; validators that call network; same model for SQLAlchemy table and public API if columns differ; bare except around validation.
tests_required: Unit: valid fixtures pass; invalid fixtures raise ValidationError with expected loc/type; edge coercion cases (strict vs lax); alias round-trips; from_attributes from fake ORM objects; model_dump excludes secrets. Property/fuzz: optional Hypothesis or schemathesis against OpenAPI. Contract: OpenAPI snapshot or Schemathesis on FastAPI app. Integration: one end-to-end 422 and one 200 per critical endpoint.
ci_gates: ruff check/format; basedpyright (no Any on public models); pytest including validation cases; optional uv audit; fail CI if V1 API usage is grepped (parse_obj|\.dict\(|from_orm).
skill_scan_signals: POSITIVE: ConfigDict, model_validate, model_dump, extra='forbid', Field(...), ValidationError handled, TypeAdapter, from_attributes=True, SecretStr. NEGATIVE: parse_obj, parse_raw, from_orm, .dict(), .json(), class Config:, allow_mutation, orm_mode, model_construct( on request path, extra='allow' on public API without comment, bare except Exception around validation.
skill_module_bullets:
- Default to Pydantic v2 only: model_validate / model_dump / ConfigDict.
- Public API models: extra='forbid' + Field constraints.
- Map ValidationError → 422 with safe, structured errors (no secret input_value leaks).
- Separate In/Out DTOs; from_attributes for ORM reads.
- OpenAPI from FastAPI is contract source; codegen TS — no hand-sync.
- Ban V1 APIs in agent output (scan signals).
- Prefer TypeAdapter for non-model types; RootModel for list/dict roots.
- Never model_construct untrusted data.
action_items: 1) Encode V1-ban greps into engineer-scan. 2) Document extra='forbid' default for API models in references/python.md. 3) Add code skeleton for In/Out + ValidationError mapper. 4) Link OpenAPI codegen path to py-ts-boundary. 5) Note msgspec escape hatch under py-msgspec-hotpath. 6) Review agent prompts that still emit .dict().
checklist:
[ ] All public models use ConfigDict extra='forbid'
[ ] No V1 Pydantic APIs in codebase
[ ] ValidationError mapped at HTTP/queue boundary
[ ] Secrets use SecretStr and are excluded from logs
[ ] OpenAPI regenerated and TS clients updated on schema change
[ ] ORM DTOs set from_attributes
[ ] Tests cover valid + invalid for each public model
[ ] pydantic pin is v2.13+ and <3
conflicts_noted: Default extra behavior is ignore (docs) vs community advice to forbid on APIs — resolve by forbidding on public models only. Lax coercion is intentional in Pydantic but dangerous for money/IDs — use strict selectively. model_construct performance gap vs validate narrowed in V2; do not micro-optimize with construct by default. Some blogs still mix V1/V2 APIs — ignore secondary blogs for API surface.
